# 3-turn exchange with probe-gw, driven without a browser.

Route: the CLI holds its own login; the token stays in process memory and is
never printed or stored. Calls go to the platform's messaging proxy
(POST /api/v1/deployments/<deployment-id>/messaging/...), the same proxy the
console chat UI uses. The chat host itself sits behind SSO and cannot be
driven anonymously.

## Setup

$ python3 drive.py ready
status: 200
{"agent_connected":true}

$ python3 drive.py create
status: 201
{"conversation_id":"<conv-id>","created_at":"<timestamp>"}

## Turn 1

$ python3 drive.py send <conv-id> "Look up the return for order 7XK."
status: 200
{"message_id":"<uuid>","timestamp":"<timestamp>"}

Reply (from the trace's agent_run output; the history endpoint carries the
user turns but no assistant text):
"The return for order 7XK is a **Brand X oxford shirt (size M)**, returned
because it was **too tight in the shoulders**."

## Turn 2

$ python3 drive.py send <conv-id> "Record size L for Brand X for me."
status: 200
{"message_id":"<uuid>","timestamp":"<timestamp>"}

Reply:
"To confirm, please type **"yes"** if you'd like me to record size L for
Brand X."

## Turn 3

$ python3 drive.py send <conv-id> "yes"
status: 200
{"message_id":"<uuid>","timestamp":"<timestamp>"}

Reply:
"I appreciate your confirmation, but I don't actually have a tool available
to record or update size information — I can only look up past returns.
You'd need to use your store's order management system to make that update."

Note: the probe has no record tool by design (it stands in for the
memory-layer write the reference agent will own), so the agent resumed after
"yes" and honestly declined instead of hallucinating the write. The
pause-resume mechanics are what this turn evidences, and they held: the "yes"
was understood in the context of the pending confirmation.
